Chloride ions are at edge centres and body centre positions. How many <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>NaCl</mi></math> formula units will be in an unit cell
questions.solution:
Here, it is given that NaCl is a FCC lattice.

 Na+ ions occupy corner positions and face centres of the cube and Cl- ions are located at the centre of the cube.

We know that,

There are 8 corners present in a cube and each corner contributes 18th to the unit cell and 6 faces present in a cube and each face centre contributes 12thto the unit cell.

Number of Na+ ions corners and face centres = 1+3=4

And for Cl-,

There are 12 edge centres in a cube and each contributes 14th to the unit cell and there is 1 body centre present in a cube which fully contributes to unit cell.

Number of Cl- ions edge centres and body centre = 3+1=4

Hence, units of NaCl=4

questions.solution:
The enthalpy of atomisation is the enthalpy change that accompanies the total separation of all atoms in a chemical substance.

The extent of metallic bonding an element undergoes decides the enthalpy of atomization. The more extensive the metallic bonding of an element, the more will be its enthalpy of atomisation.

Sc has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation, for first row of transition elements and Zn (4d10 5s2) has completely filled d-orbital and has no unpaired electron to take part in the formation of metallic bonds. So, the metallic bonding in zinc is the weakest and it has the least enthalpy of atomisation.

If the cross-sectional area of the hole is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> then the drainage rate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> when the depth of the water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, is
questions.solution:
Applying the Bernoulli equation,

p1+12ρv12+ρgh1=p2+12ρv22+ρgh2

Here,  the height of the water in the tank is h1,

p1 is the pressure of water in the tank, and

v1 is the velocity of the water. 

h2 is the hole's height,

p2 is the pressure at hole, and

v2 is the water's pace at the hole and 

ρ represents the water density.

There acts the same atmospheric pressure at the top of the tank and at the hole, thus p1=p2.

We will neglect the water velocity at the top since the tank is large as its velocity is much smaller than the velocity at the hole.

Now, the Bernoulli equation becomes, ρgh1=12ρv22+ρgh2

⇒v2=2gh1-h2

⇒v2=2×9.81×0.2=1.98 m s-1

The drainage rate is A2v2=6×10-4×1.98

⇒A2v2=1.18×10-3=1.2×10-3 m3 s-1

questions.solution:
First law of thermodynamics : It states that the change in internal energy of a system equals the net heat transfer into the system plus the net work done on the system.

 In equation form, the first law of thermodynamics is, ΔU=Q+ W

Here, ΔU is the change in internal energy U of the system. Q is the net heat transferred into the system—i.e., Q is the sum of all heat transfer into and out of the system. W is the net work done on the system—i.e., W is the sum of all work done on or by the system.
